intro_en: This is the last lesson of your N5 journey. You will learn the conditional 〜たら ('if it rains tomorrow'), 〜ても ('even if it rains'), いくら〜ても ('no matter how hard I try'), つもり ('I intend to') and 予定 ('a plan / schedule'). They work just like the Tamil verb endings '-ஆல்' (if) and '-ஆலும்' (even if), so they should feel easy. Finally, we will look back with a complete map of what the て, ない, dictionary and た forms you have learned so far each do.

g25-1.explanation_en: Add ら to the た-form from Lesson 19 and you get the conditional form: 降った → 降ったら (if it rains). It has two meanings: (1) 'if by chance ... happens': 雨が降ったら、行きません (if it rains, I won’t go). (2) 'after something that will surely happen is finished': 駅に着いたら、電話してください (when you arrive at the station, please call me). It is a direct match for the Tamil endings '-ஆல்' (if) and '-ஆனதும்' (as soon as). Negative: 〜なかったら (if ... doesn’t come / happen). い-adjectives: 安かったら; な-adjectives and nouns: 暇だったら、雨だったら. Unlike と from Lesson 23, たら can be followed by a wish, a command or an invitation: 〜たら、〜てください / 〜ましょう / 〜たいです. That is why this is the most useful conditional in everyday speech.
g25-1.tamil_parallel_en: மழை பெய்தால் போகமாட்டேன் (if it rains, I won’t go) = 雨が降ったら、行きません ； ஸ்டேஷனை அடைந்ததும் போன் செய்யுங்கள் (when you reach the station, please call) = 駅に着いたら、電話してください. Tamil -ஆல் (பெய்தால்) and -ஆனதும் (அடைந்ததும்) are both covered by たら.
g25-1.formation_en: V た-form + ら ； V なかった + ら ； い-adj かった + ら ； な-adj / N + だった + ら
g25-1.pitfalls_en: Putting the dictionary form before たら is wrong: ×降るたら → ○降ったら. Nouns need だった: ×雨たら → ○雨だったら.

g25-2.explanation_en: 'Even if it rains, I will go' — to say that the result goes against what you would expect, use て-form + も. It is a direct match for Tamil '-ஆலும்' (பெய்தாலும் 'even if it rains', சாப்பிட்டாலும் 'even if I eat'); and just like the Tamil 'உம்', Japanese も also means 'even / also'! 降って → 降っても、食べて → 食べても. い-adjectives: 高い → 高くても (even if it is expensive). な-adjectives and nouns: 暇 → 暇でも、雨 → 雨でも. Negative: 〜なくても (the form you saw in なくてもいいです in Lesson 17). 〜てもいいですか (may I do it?) from Lesson 15 also comes from this same form: 'is it all right even if I do it?'
g25-2.tamil_parallel_en: மழை பெய்தாலும் போவேன் (even if it rains, I will go) = 雨が降っても、行きます. て-form + も = Tamil -ஆலும், and both も and உம் carry the sense of 'even'.
g25-2.formation_en: V て-form + も ； V なくて + も ； い-adj くて + も ； な-adj / N + でも
g25-2.pitfalls_en: Saying 高いでも for an い-adjective is wrong: ○高くても. Don’t confuse 〜ても with 〜たら: ても = 'even if' (an unexpected result), たら = 'if' (a natural result).

g25-3.explanation_en: Both of these are helper words that come at the start of a sentence and signal in advance which form is coming later. (1) もし + 〜たら: stresses the condition, 'if by chance': もし雨が降ったら (if by chance it rains). It matches Tamil 'ஒருவேளை' (perhaps / if by chance). The meaning doesn’t change without もし, but the listener knows from the start that 'a condition is coming'. (2) いくら + 〜ても: 'no matter how much ...'. You learned いくら in Lesson 3 as 'how much (price)'; together with ても it means 'however much': いくら勉強しても、漢字は難しいです. It is a direct match for Tamil 'எவ்வளவு படித்தாலும்' (no matter how much I study). いくら must always be followed by ても (not たら).
g25-3.tamil_parallel_en: ஒருவேளை மழை பெய்தால் (if by chance it rains) = もし雨が降ったら ； எவ்வளவு படித்தாலும் (no matter how much I study) = いくら勉強しても. Tamil ஒருவேளை matches もし, and எவ்வளவு ... -ஆலும் matches いくら ... ても.
g25-3.formation_en: もし + 〜たら、〜 ； いくら + V て-form / い-adj くて / N で + も、〜
g25-3.pitfalls_en: ×いくら勉強したら is wrong; いくら only goes with ても. After もし, the natural form is 〜たら, not 〜ても.

g25-4.explanation_en: To talk about a decision or intention in your mind, use dictionary form + つもりです: 来年日本へ行くつもりです (I intend to go to Japan next year). It matches Tamil 'போக எண்ணியிருக்கிறேன்' (I intend to go) and 'போகலாம் என்று இருக்கிறேன்' (I’m thinking of going). For 'intend not to do', use ない-form + つもりです: たばこを吸わないつもりです. Since つもり is a noun, the 'sentence + noun' rule from Lesson 22 works here. 〜たいです from Lesson 13 is only a 'wish'; つもり is a 'decided intention'. Asking a superior directly 'what do you intend to do?' with つもりですか can sound a little harsh.
g25-4.tamil_parallel_en: அடுத்த ஆண்டு ஜப்பான் போக எண்ணியிருக்கிறேன் (I intend to go to Japan next year) = 来年日本へ行くつもりです. Tamil infinitive + எண்ணியிருக்கிறேன் (I have in mind) matches dictionary form + つもりです.
g25-4.formation_en: V dictionary form + つもりです ； V ない-form + つもりです
g25-4.pitfalls_en: The ます-form or たい does not come before つもり: ×行きますつもり、×行きたいつもり → ○行くつもり.

g25-5.explanation_en: 予定 (よてい) means 'plan, schedule'. つもり is an intention in your mind; 予定 is a decided event, written on the calendar and known to others. Dictionary form + 予定です: 来月結婚する予定です (the wedding is planned for next month). Noun + の + 予定です: 旅行の予定です. It is also used for schedules that are 'not in our hands', such as trains, flights and meetings: 電車は十時に着く予定です. It matches Tamil 'திட்டம்' (plan) and 'ஏற்பாடு' (arrangement). 'Do you have any plans?' = 何か予定がありますか.
g25-5.tamil_parallel_en: அடுத்த மாதம் திருமணம் நடக்கத் திட்டம் (the wedding is planned for next month) = 来月結婚する予定です ； நாளை மறுநாள் பயணத் திட்டம் (the day after tomorrow, I have a trip planned) = 明後日は旅行の予定です. Tamil திட்டம் (plan) placed after a verb or noun works like 予定.
g25-5.formation_en: V dictionary form + 予定です ； N + の + 予定です ； 予定が あります
g25-5.pitfalls_en: Don’t forget の after a noun: ×旅行予定です (you sometimes hear this in speech, but for N5 use の) → ○旅行の予定です.

g25-6.explanation_en: Throughout N5 you learned five forms of a verb. Let’s see in one place what each one does (using 行く as the example). ① ます-form (行きます): the polite sentence ending; its stem (行き) + たい (wish), ながら (while), ましょう/ましょうか, に行く (go to do). ② て-form (行って): like the Tamil verbal participle 'போய்' (having gone) — てください (request), ている (in progress / state), てもいい (permission), てはいけない (prohibition), てから (after), て、て (sequence), てあげる/くれる/もらう (favours), ても (even if). ③ ない-form (行かない): like Tamil 'போகாத' (not going) — ないでください (please don’t), なければなりません (must), なくてもいい (don’t have to), ないつもり. ④ Dictionary form (行く): ことができる (can), ことです (hobby), 前に (before), と (natural result), つもり, 予定, describing a noun (行く人), と思う, 時. ⑤ た-form (行った): たことがある (experience), たり〜たり (listing), たほうがいい (advice), たあとで (after), たら (condition), た時, 行った人 (past relative form). It is just like how Tamil makes many forms from one verb: 'போய்', 'போகாத', 'போகும்', 'போன', 'போனால்'. In plain style (Lesson 20), forms ④, ⑤ and ③ also serve as sentence endings.
g25-6.tamil_parallel_en: போய் (having gone, て) / போகாத (not going, ない) / போகும் (that goes, dictionary) / போன (that went, た) / போனால் (if I go, たら) / போனாலும் (even if I go, ても) = 行って / 行かない / 行く / 行った / 行ったら / 行っても. Like Tamil, Japanese builds all these meanings from one verb by changing its ending.
g25-6.formation_en: ます-stem: たい・ながら・ましょう ； て: ください・いる・もいい・はいけない・から・あげる/くれる/もらう・も ； ない: でください・ければなりません・くてもいい ； dictionary: ことができる・前に・と・つもり・予定・時・+N ； た: ことがある・り〜たり・ほうがいい・あとで・ら・時・+N
g25-6.pitfalls_en: When choosing a form, look at 'what comes after it': て or ないで before ください, た before ことがある, the dictionary form before ことができる. ×行くことがあります (a different meaning: 'I sometimes go') ≠ ○行ったことがあります (the experience of having gone).

items.L25-q01: 明後日 = あさって (நாளை மறுநாள், the day after tomorrow), a special reading. あさて is missing the small っ. みょうごにち is the formal form; in N5 only あさって is used.
items.L25-q02: 大学 = だいがく (பல்கலைக்கழகம், university). Here 大 is voiced as だい; it is not たい as in 大切 (たいせつ) — that is the main trap. 学 is がく in compounds.
items.L25-q03: 緑 = みどり (பச்சை, green). みとり has lost the voicing. あお (青) can sometimes mean green in Japan, but it is not the reading of this kanji.
items.L25-q04: らいげつ = 来月 (அடுத்த மாதம், next month). 来年 (らいねん) and 来週 (らいしゅう) sound different. 末 is a fake that looks like 来.
items.L25-q05: はんぶん = 半分 (பாதி, half). 反 (はん) is a different kanji with the same sound; 今 (いま) looks like 分; 羊 is a fake that looks like 半.
items.L25-q06: Time or money 'takes / costs' = かかります (ஆகும், takes). あります would change the meaning to 'there is one hour'; なります means 'becomes (changes)'.
items.L25-q07: To say the exact time, use 丁度 (சரியாக, exactly). 多分 (probably) doesn’t fit a time you read off a clock; だんだん (gradually) and なかなか (not easily) don’t fit the meaning.
items.L25-q08: 外に (ほかに) = (வேறு, இதைத் தவிர, anything else / besides this). 全部に or 自分に make no sense here. The same kanji is also read そと (outside) — choose the reading by the meaning.
items.L25-q09: 自分で = (தானே, சொந்தமாக, by oneself / on one’s own). 一人で means 'alone' (without others) — the meaning is close, but for the emphasis 'my own room, by myself' use 自分で. 家庭で (at home) shows a place.
items.L25-q10: 色々な国 = (பல நாடுகள், various countries). 大切な (important) and 丈夫な (sturdy) are also な-adjectives, but they don’t fit with 'food of the countries'.
items.L25-q11: Five minutes past nine = 'past' nine → 九時すぎ (தாண்டி, past). 前 (before) is the exact opposite; 半 would mean half past nine; まで (until) makes no sense here. もう (already) also shows that the time has 'passed'.
items.L25-q12: さ来年 = (அடுத்த ஆண்டுக்கு அடுத்த ஆண்டு, the year after next) = 来年の次の年; つもり = an intention in your mind ≈ 〜たいと思っています. 来月 (next month) is the wrong time; 来年/去年 with the past tense are wrong.
items.L25-q13: 'No matter how long I waited, it didn’t come' = I waited a long time, but it didn’t come (வரவில்லை). The second option, 'it came after I waited a little', is the exact opposite.
items.L25-q14: なくてもいい (தேவையில்லை, don’t have to) = 終わらなくても大丈夫 (முடியாவிட்டாலும் பரவாயில்லை, it’s fine even if it isn’t finished). The first option, なければなりません (must), is the exact opposite and a common trap.
items.L25-q15: 'If it rains, I won’t climb the mountain' = 降ったら (பெய்தால், if it rains). 降っても would mean 'even if it rains, I won’t climb', which is contradictory. 降るので means 'because it will rain' — as if it were certain.
items.L25-q16: Taking a walk even in the rain goes against expectation → 降っても (பெய்தாலும், even if it rains). 降ったら, 'if it rains, (because of that) I take a walk', is unnatural; 降る時 means 'when it rains', which doesn’t fit with 毎朝 (every morning).
items.L25-q17: いくら always goes with ても: いくら練習しても (எவ்வளவு பயிற்சி செய்தாலும், no matter how much I practise) I don’t get good at kanji. いくら〜たら is a wrong combination; 練習すると means 'if you practise (naturally)', which contradicts the meaning.
items.L25-q18: An intention in your mind: dictionary form + つもりです (எண்ணம், intention). 〜ほうです or 〜ことです are not used with this meaning (ことです only appears in the 'my hobby is X' pattern).
items.L25-q19: Noun + の + 予定: 旅行の予定です (பயணத் திட்டம், a trip is planned). な is only for な-adjectives; with に the link breaks and it means 'for the trip'.
items.L25-q20: Because a request (〜てください) comes after it, it must be たら: 着いたら (அடைந்ததும், when you arrive). A request cannot come after と (Lesson 23) — that is the main trap.
items.L25-q21: い-adjective + ても = 広くても (விசாலமாக இருந்தாலும், even if it is spacious). 広いでも wrongly applies the な-adjective rule. 広くて would mean 'because it is spacious', which contradicts the meaning.
items.L25-q22: た-form + ことがあります = experience (அனுபவம்) (Lesson 19). つもり/予定 need the dictionary form before them, not the た-form.
items.L25-q23: もし お金が たくさん あったら、何を しますか。 — もし + the condition (〜たら) comes first, then the question. あったら goes in the star position.
items.L25-q24: 大学を 出たら、日本の 会社で 働く つもりです。 — The condition, then the place (日本の 会社で), and at the end the dictionary form 働く + つもりです. 働く goes in the star position.
items.L25-q25: これは 母が 毎年 作って くれる お菓子です。 — (இது அம்மா ஒவ்வொரு ஆண்டும் செய்து தரும் இனிப்பு, these are the sweets my mother makes for me every year). The subject of the inner clause takes が (Lesson 22), and てくれる (Lesson 24) describes the noun. 母が goes in the star position.
items.L25-q26: ［1］ 'Even though I study every day, it is still hard' — against expectation → しても. ［2］ Dictionary form 働く + つもりです (intention). 予定の is a form error. ［3］ もし + たら: 'if by chance I make friends'; because a wish (〜たいです) comes after it, と doesn’t fit.
